The continuation restated the corrected child-and-parent 85/85 gate and noted that occasional non-memory toss-up assignments may be issued later under Supervisor.md override 7.

When a child clears 85/85 and the only assignment blocker is a plausible direct parent below 85/85, associated-parent improvement is mandatory before reporting `reviewed-no-85`, unless the parent is leased, not a direct owner, or cannot be justifiably improved. Agent-A002 also received a specific follow-up to revisit `0002OT` VirusChecker parent confidence.
- By-structure clarification: Updated `Supervisor.md` override 9 and queued the same instruction to all active agents. The temporary batch override changes target selection only; normal by-structure rules still apply, including splitting/renaming mixed or overbroad memory ranges when evidence supports a clean split.
- 12:31 ET: Agent-A001 and Agent-A007 repeatedly returned empty completed statuses after explicit resume and input. Replaced only those two unrecoverable sessions while preserving folder/batch mapping: Agent-A001 Batch 045 is now session `019ea31a-fac5-75c1-b9f5-c7f5c2c123c9` (Herschel), and Agent-A007 Batch 041 is now session `019ea31a-fb5d-7933-881e-f895167d90a6` (Mencius).

- New split-file leasing clarification: Updated `Supervisor.md` override 10 and notified agents that non-existent child files cannot be leased. Agents must lease the existing parent item being split, create new child files while holding that parent-item lease, then validate and update reports/notes.
- Failed split-work recovery: Added note-derived failed split items to the split-recheck queue, including `0002AE`, `00017F`, `0001C3`, `0000ZM`, `000174`, `0001MT`, `0001L8`, `00016J`, and `00016L`.

All by-structure, validator, lease, naming/renaming, coverage, and quality rules remain active, and agents should repair discovered range/file/parent/score/coverage issues when possible.

- Usage-limit recovery: The replacement Agent-A001/Agent-A007 sessions hit account usage limits and were not usable. After the user reported limits were removed, the original ten sessions were resumed and current batches were reissued, preserving the original one-folder-per-agent mapping.
